title: The bottom number counts all the equal parts
concept: A fraction names equal parts of ONE whole. The bottom number is how many equal parts the whole is cut into, all of them, shaded or not.
The top number is how many of those parts we mean. So the fraction of a shape that is shaded is (shaded parts) over (all the equal parts).

alternative.title: Whole first
text: Before naming a fraction, say what the whole is and how many equal parts it has.

members.title: Naming a shaded fraction: out of ALL the equal parts
Shading a fraction of a grid: parts of the whole, not the top number

crossDiagnostic.case: grid larger than the bottom number

responsePatterns.supports: names the fraction part-to-part (shaded over unshaded) while shading a given fraction is right
responsePatterns.uncertain: a conceptual part-to-part reading of naming, or a habit only in naming tasks; one answer: suspected only

responsePatterns.supports: names fractions but reads the top number as squares when shading
responsePatterns.uncertain: the size of a part in a bigger whole; fix_top_number

responsePatterns.supports: fractions treated as plain counts in both directions
responsePatterns.uncertain: the two answers are different errors, and typing only the top number also explains the first; teach the shared concept as general teaching, but do NOT establish either misconception from this pair
